name: Clinical Decision Support Software
blurb: When decision support AI is regulated as a device.
title: Clinical Decision Support Software
answer: Whether clinical decision support software is regulated by the FDA depends on its intended use. Under the FDA's 2022 guidance, software that lets a clinician independently review the basis for a recommendation can fall outside device rules, while tools that analyse images or signals, or drive time critical decisions, are regulated devices.

reading.body:
Whether clinical decision support software is regulated as a medical device turns on intended use, not on whether AI is involved. The FDA's 2022 guidance draws the line at clinician review: software that lets a clinician independently review the basis for a recommendation can fall outside device rules, while tools that analyse images or signals, or drive time critical decisions, are regulated devices.

The distinction is about who holds the judgment. A tool that surfaces a recommendation and the reasoning behind it leaves the clinician able to accept or reject it, so the software is treated as supporting rather than deciding. A tool that reads an image or a signal, or that must act inside a time critical window, has already made the call, and that is what makes it a device.

For AI specifically, this means the regulatory burden follows the output, not the model. Two systems built on similar methods can land on opposite sides of the line if one explains itself to a clinician and the other does not. The practical question for a care team is whether a vendor's tool is FDA authorized or relies on the non-device criteria, and what evidence each path requires.

The data covers the rule and its criteria. It does not cover how many tools fall on either side, how enforcement has gone, or what the cited literature found.
